title: Abstraction (computer science)
summary: Abstraction in computer science provides access to functionality while concealing implementation details that would otherwise complicate usage. It allows programmers to focus on contextually relevant information by filtering out irrelevant specifics. The concept applies across language levels, from low-level machine operations to high-level design patterns, enabling manageable system creation through layered separation of concerns.

mechanisms.title: Interface-Implementation Separation
mechanisms.explanation: Abstract data types enforce a clear separation between visible properties and hidden concrete implementation. Client code interacts through a defined interface while the underlying representation—such as hash tables, binary trees, or lists—can change without affecting usage, preserving abstract behavior regardless of implementation details.

mechanisms.title: Control Abstraction Layering
mechanisms.explanation: Programming languages provide higher-level control structures that obscure low-level hardware operations. Arithmetic expressions are evaluated through compiler or interpreter decomposition into binary operations, allowing programmers to write intuitive statements without manually managing register manipulations, binary conversions, or memory assignment steps for each calculation.
